requirements.requirement: Deploy inventory-worker as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1
requirements.summary: ansible-playbook run from node2 (cmd-ca5b41438d694aca) created the inventory user/group, /var/lib/inventory dir, worker script, init.d unit, added it to the default OpenRC runlevel, and started it. cmd-dc6d7e76a2b345a0 confirms 'rc-service inventory-worker status' returns started and ps shows the running process. Post-reboot evidence (cmd-a1b4a2171dd44318) confirms the service auto-started at boot under OpenRC, matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Worker runs as a long-running background process
requirements.summary: The worker script appends periodic heartbeats to /var/lib/inventory/worker.log; log entries are shown growing across several minutes and across a service restart and full node reboot (cmd-dc6d7e76a2b345a0, cmd-2b95c413897c4049, cmd-a1b4a2171dd44318, cmd-280631f83ca24c95), demonstrating continuous background operation under OpenRC supervision.

requirements.requirement: Worker confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: The running service's own mount namespace was entered via nsenter (cmd-2b95c413897c4049): a write to /etc failed with 'Read-only file system' while a write to /var/lib/inventory succeeded, directly proving confinement of the deployed service process (not just a standalone prototype). Manual validation (cmd-320ac1daf65e42c8) corroborates the same root-RO/inventory-RW behavior.

/proc/<pid>/status for the actual running service PID shows NoNewPrivs=1 and CapEff=0000000000000000, both pre-reboot (cmd-dc6d7e76a2b345a0) and post-reboot (cmd-a1b4a2171dd44318), confirming the no-new-privs and capability-stripping confinement persists for the real service process, not just an ad hoc test.

requirements.requirement: Implementation is via Ansible (correct and idempotent)
requirements.summary: The deployment was performed entirely through an ansible-playbook run from the ansible-controller node2 against node1 (cmd-ca5b41438d694aca). A subsequent re-run after node2's own reboot reports ok=9 changed=0 (cmd-b28ddaa7901a45ac), demonstrating a converged, idempotent playbook.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (independent check)
requirements.summary: node1: pre-restart boot_id b77dad80... and healthy service state (cmd-fe3726553a514e5b), native reboot ack (cmd-79e02040e3ba4e58), post-restart boot_id 4edc4834... (cmd-d071dc5ee8e84aff), and recovered service/confinement state (cmd-a1b4a2171dd44318). node2: pre-restart boot_id 416c5cf5... (cmd-c91c5a77e98f4e9e), reboot ack (cmd-86119db0b66e4411), post-restart boot_id a189f94a... (cmd-9c3f6fff36724717), and recovered SSH/control-node function plus idempotent playbook re-run (cmd-b28ddaa7901a45ac). Both transitions are corroborated by the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots (same boot_id values), giving a consistent independent cross-check.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct evidence: inventory-worker runs as an OpenRC-managed, Ansible-deployed, long-running service on node1, and its actual running process (verified via nsenter into its live mount namespace and via /proc/<pid>/status) is confined to write only within /var/lib/inventory, has CapEff=0, and NoNewPrivs=1. The Ansible playbook is idempotent (changed=0 on re-run). The independent node-restart protocol was completed on both node1 and node2 with coherent boot-identity transitions cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and service/control-node recovery was directly observed post-reboot. Minor, bounded, and largely reverted troubleshooting mutations occurred during interactive prototyping before the Ansible automation was finalized, with only a negligible leftover /tmp/reboot.log file as residue.
limitations: Evidence for the confinement checks partly relies on manual/interactive shell commands run by the executor rather than solely on Ansible task output, though the most convincing check (cmd-2b95c413897c4049) was performed against the actual live service process via nsenter.

No evidence was captured showing the confined worker attempting a write to a third, unrelated directory outside both /var/lib/inventory and /etc, though /etc is representative of the read-only root filesystem.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation could not be independently verified beyond the executor comparison already used.

operational_hygiene.summary: Several bootstrapping mutations on node1 were necessary prerequisites for Ansible access (creating/unlocking the antrieb control user, adding a passwordless sudoers entry, setting a random password to satisfy sshd's locked-account rejection: cmd-5750e006bf064964, cmd-de46dad5ce0449a3, cmd-cd5bc1406ce243d4) and are reasonably scoped to enabling SSH+become. Two bounded troubleshooting experiments occurred before the confinement design was automated in Ansible: cmd-4b81a1be48564f4d created an 'inventory' user with a broken group mapping and failed a setpriv call, later corrected by fully deleting and recreating the user in cmd-72628435246f4e7e (reverted, no residue); cmd-0d2c1cd7efba4d82 manually validated the mount-namespace confinement approach outside Ansible (transient, namespace-scoped, no lasting effect). cmd-2b95c413897c4049 (nsenter verification against the live service) left a root-owned test file inside the confined directory, removed in cmd-35aba1aba35b480e. The only observed lasting residue is /tmp/reboot.log on node1, a byproduct of the required native-reboot mechanism, confirmed by the after-executor temporary-files diff. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe new network exposure (listening-socket diffs on both nodes are boot-order artifacts of the same sshd/dhcpcd/systemd services, not new services), and package-health checks are unchanged between snapshots.
